items.title: Billy Taylor — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So he went over to the Steinway Hall with me

ctx.x: start packing up and getting back and get something to eat and clean up and go to work at 9:00 p.m. Everybody else is out. Everybody else is like I am going to relax. I’m having a good day at the beach. But I have to get up and go to work. That was just a part of… it was something that I enjoyed doing. It was an important part of my life. But it was different from many other guys who would hang out all night and go to the after hour places I had done when I was younger and before I got married. And I must confess…

Coming back to the period I am talking about in the mid 50’s and not only were there musical changes but there were changes in society. You had the Emma Till incident in Mississippi. You had Rosa Parks in Montgomery and then in 1957 you had Brown vs. the Board of Education… 1954, I’m sorry. What were… this is a two part question. What were black audiences like with jazz and what was your motivation for writing an article about what you felt about Negroes at that time, knowing about the music?
